artists.biography: Pop Will Eat Itself (also known as PWEI or The Poppies) are an English alternative rock band, originally formed in Stourbridge in 1986, with members from Birmingham, Coventry and the Black Country. Initially known as a Grebo act, their style changed to incorporate sample driven indie and industrial rock. Their highest charting single was 1993's "Get The Girl! Kill The Baddies!". After initially disbanding in 1996, and having a brief reformation in 2005, they issued their first release in over five years in 2010.

perplexity.description:
Delete Everything," released in 2025, is the eighth studio album by British band Pop Will Eat Itself, self-released under their own imprint Not On Label. The album marks a return after a decade-long hiatus and showcases a refined fusion of electronic music with elements of industrial rock, techno, hip hop, and punk. Its sound is characterized by high-energy, hypnotic rhythms, heavy beats, and a collage-like approach to genre blending, with vocals shared dynamically between Graham Crabb and Mary Byker. Instrumentation includes aggressive guitar work, bass, programming, and energetic drumming, creating a chaotic yet captivating sonic landscape that evokes a dystopian, sci-fi atmosphere.

Within Pop Will Eat Itself's discography, "Delete Everything" represents both a continuation and reinvention of their signature style, embracing modern electronic textures while retaining their punk and industrial roots. Tracks like "Bruiser" and "Their Law (Ain't Our Law)" have been highlighted for their anthemic qualities and live appeal, with the latter being a reimagined fan favorite that blends heavy guitars and techno elements. The album closes on a more optimistic note with "Where There's Hope," showcasing the vocal interplay and melodic versatility of the band.

Critically, the album has been praised for its inventive energy and refusal to conform to mainstream expectations, reaffirming Pop Will Eat Itself's reputation for creative restlessness and genre-defying music. It has been described as a "techno tornado" and a "soundtrack to a dystopian rebellion," with particular acclaim for its fresh ideas and physical, danceable intensity. Commercially, it has supported a robust touring schedule in 2025, reinforcing the band's enduring appeal and live performance strength.
